newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Old Mutual sees more trade with Africa.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Old Mutual sees more trade with Africa.

text.p: South African trade with other countries in Africa will continue to grow and could account for up to 25 percent of exports within about 10 years, Old Mutual Unit Trusts economist Erika Prinsloo said on Tuesday.
Prinsloo, who has just completed a study of investment opportunities in southern and central Africa, told Reuters the main growth would be in the export of manufactured goods.
"I would say the opportunity lies in foods, consumer goods and machinery and equipment, roughly in that order," she said.
"South Africa has almost doubled its exports to other African countries from around $2 billion in 1993 to $3.7 billion in 1996," she said.
Exports into the rest of the continent accounted for around 15 percent of total exports, including gold, she said.

"I don't think we can expect another doubling in the short to medium term, but I think it is possible that the African share of South African exports could rise to 25 percent in the next 10 years or so," she said.
Prinsloo cited Mozambique and Angola as immediate targets for exports and South African investment because both had to recover from severe devastation caused by civil war.
"The opportunity lies in a combination of helping countries to recover from devastation and in establishing manufacturing in slightly more sophisticated economies.

"I think we need to look at investing in countries to the north to manufacture there, taking advantage of lower labour costs, and then import the finished products to the South African market," she said.
"There is definitely the potential to do more than just help to rebuild shattered infrastructure.
"Renewal on its doorstep is lifting South Africa's growth potential...Sugar, beer and clothing manufacturers have set up plant and sales throughout the Southern African region and more will follow."
Prinsloo said she undertook the study for Old Mutual, the country's biggest investment institution, to assess the potential for accelerated trade.
"For so long, Africa has just been ignored. We need to reassess our view of the continent and its potential for investment. There is just so much opportunity throughout the continent," she said.
